objective: The paper shows that a learned temporal policy is necessary but says nothing about why THIS head. Three design decisions have never been ablated: the 64 frozen ResNet-18 appearance channels, the learned stereo evidence block as a whole, and the convex-fusion constraint on the output. The last is the sharpest gap, because the Analysis section already asserts that convexity is a plausible reason the head transfers to unseen backbones, and that assertion currently has no experiment behind it.

A1_no_appearance_channels.change: drop the 64 tanh-compressed frozen ResNet-18 layer1 channels from the 142-channel cue stack, leaving 78
A1_no_appearance_channels.rationale: Appearance self-correlation and cross-appearance correlation are already derived from those same features. This asks whether raw appearance adds anything BEYOND the correlations computed from it.
A1_no_appearance_channels.honest_note: This does NOT remove the frozen extractor from the runtime: the appearance correlations still require it. Only the input width of the first convolution shrinks. Any latency claim belongs to A2, not here.

A2_no_learned_stereo_evidence.change: 142 -> 38 channels: removes confidence curves, their supports, both appearance correlations and the ResNet block, leaving disparity/motion/RGB geometry
A2_no_learned_stereo_evidence.rationale: Tests whether the head needs learned features at all. This is the variant that removes the frozen extractor from the deployed system, so it is the one with a runtime consequence.
A2_no_learned_stereo_evidence.implementation: an existing flag in train.py; no code change

A4_relaxed_convexity.change: add a zero-initialised 1x1 convolution on the coarse branch whose output is ADDED to the convex blend, so the head can place its prediction outside the [raw, aligned memory] interval
A4_relaxed_convexity.rationale: Minimal relaxation of the convexity constraint. Removing the sigmoid from fusion_weight instead would have been unfair: the loss supervises that weight as a probability and an unbounded weight makes those terms degenerate, so we would be ablating the loss and not the architecture.
A4_relaxed_convexity.initialisation: zero, so training starts exactly at the canonical model and any departure from convexity is learned rather than imposed
A4_relaxed_convexity.honest_note: This relaxes the constraint, it does not remove it. A head that never uses the extrapolation term is evidence FOR convexity; one that does is evidence against.

unchanged_and_verified_at_launch.checkpoint_selection_rule: best development (D2) fused EPE, identical to the canonical run

protocol.implementation: model_design/train_ablation.py, a sibling of train.py that reuses its metadata(), verify_sources(), validate_output() and config() unchanged and patches only the runner's cue builder or head class
protocol.evaluation: each checkpoint is evaluated with the frozen support-masked module on SCARED-C D2 and D7 under the unmodified definitive protocol; no threshold, policy or selection rule is re-tuned
protocol.reporting_rule: report the relative Bad1 and EPE reduction of each variant against the same raw predictions, on both splits, and state the held-out D7 number as primary; a variant that matches the canonical model within the three-seed spread (0.37 percentage points pooled Bad1) is reported as indistinguishable, not as better or worse

declared_before_seeing_results.what_would_falsify_the_convexity_claim: If A4 matches or beats the canonical model on held-out D7, the Analysis sentence attributing transfer to the convex action space must be withdrawn rather than softened.
declared_before_seeing_results.what_would_make_A1_a_positive_result: If A1 matches the canonical model within the seed spread, the 64 appearance channels are redundant given their own correlations and should be dropped from the architecture description.
declared_before_seeing_results.seed_spread_is_the_yardstick: The canonical three-seed pooled Bad1 spread is 0.37 percentage points; differences smaller than that are not interpreted.

prohibited: selecting the best ablation and presenting it as the canonical model
re-tuning any threshold after seeing ablation results
changing the checkpoint-selection rule for a variant
reporting an ablation only on the split where it looks better
interpreting differences smaller than the three-seed spread
